Audit pass 1 only: contracts, Schemas, brands, errors, Config, Layers, adapters, secret-negative telemetry and boundary semantics. Re-probe all prior issues:
- Photon no provider strings; hostile getters/Proxies/descriptors cannot bypass safe typed failure/logging.
- Codex function parameters object-root recursive JSON.
- raw HTTP, request mapper, stream mapper, byte streams absent from root/runtime supported exports and built exported/test Layer contexts.
- shared SSE parser: exact media type; incremental bytes; per-line and aggregate 1 MiB bounds; correct multiline framing; malformed/unterminated/truncated rejection; constant-size proof fold; receivedStreamEvents accuracy.
- live stream emits incrementally and remains cancellable, but finish_reason/[DONE] only after framed decoded response.completed.
- app live/local/test composition.
Look for adjacent new pass-1 defects. Findings first with severity and exact file:line consequence. If none, explicitly say no findings, list invariants and residual limits. Conclude promptly; do not run broad later-pass review.

I’ll audit the specified worktree in place, beginning with repository state and the routed documentation/skills. I’ll keep the scope to pass 1 boundary semantics and re-run the prior issue probes without modifying files or contacting providers.

The target worktree is already dirty with the candidate changes, so I’m treating that exact state as the audit subject and will not alter it. The routed active owner is the Effect-native runtime SPEC/task/plan set; I’m reading those alongside the two required skills and local Effect v4 reference metadata before inspecting implementation.

The intended corrections are concentrated in Photon’s SDK-failure observer and Codex’s contracts, private SSE framer, runtime exports, and proxy composition. I’m now tracing those code paths from public exports through built Layer contexts and app mode wiring, then I’ll run only focused pass-1 tests and type/build checks needed to validate the stated invariants.

The core corrections are present, but one Photon invariant is not yet closed: the diagnostic accepts any provider-controlled safe integer as a “transport status,” so telemetry is still unbounded/high-cardinality despite the task requiring a bounded, secret-negative observation. I’m checking whether the focused suites expose any additional semantic gap, especially standard SSE framing and the app/test Layer output contracts.
Conclude now with findings or explicit no-findings and residual limits. Stop further exploration.

**Findings**

1. **High**: The aggregate 1 MiB SSE event bound is bypassable. Non-`data:` lines do not update event byte state at [sse.ts:182](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/sse.ts:182), while only stripped data payloads are counted at [sse.ts:199](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/sse.ts:199). A read-only probe successfully parsed one event containing two 600 KB comment lines plus `response.completed`. An upstream can therefore send an unbounded event block of comments or ignored fields, defeating the stated resource ceiling.

2. **Medium**: Photon telemetry still accepts arbitrary provider-controlled integers. [client.ts:98](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/photon/src/client.ts:98) accepts every safe integer from `cause.code`, and [sdk-observed-failure.ts:24](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/photon/src/sdk-observed-failure.ts:24) permits every integer. Numeric identifiers or sentinels can consequently enter structured logs, so the diagnostic is not demonstrably bounded, low-cardinality, or secret-negative. Constrain this to the admitted transport-status range or map it to `unknown`.

3. **Medium**: The shared parser rejects valid CR-only SSE framing. [sse.ts:105](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/sse.ts:105) recognizes only LF delimiters; a valid `data: ...\r\r` stream fails as an incomplete line. This makes live/proof behavior dependent on one legal SSE newline form.

Focused checks passed: Photon typecheck and 43 tests; Codex typecheck and 32 selected tests; proxy typecheck and 29 selected tests; `git diff --check`. I did not run the broad verification/build or contact providers. The local Effect reference resolved to `1caab3cc30f626efbf15e59d74f539a487e5c85c`.
